transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brought you in to see me today?
I keep having these moments where my house or my office feels unreal. Like I’m there, but not really there—almost like I’m watching myself from across the room instead of actually being in it.
During these episodes, do you also experience a sudden rush of intense fear along with things like a racing heart, shortness of breath, or sweating?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed a rush of fear or those physical things when it happens.
During these episodes, do you ever lose awareness of your surroundings, black out, or have trouble remembering what happened afterward?

I don’t black out, but there’s a part I can’t remember. I remember him crowding me in my office, and then the police being there, but what he said right before I reached for the phone is just blank. I can’t pull it up no matter how hard I try.
During these episodes, have you or anyone else noticed any unusual body movements, like jerking or repetitive motions, or things like biting your tongue or losing bladder control?
No, I haven’t noticed anything like that, and nobody’s mentioned seeing me do anything unusual.
Do these episodes of feeling unreal tend to happen specifically when something reminds you of that incident with him, or do they also occur at random times unrelated to that event?
It can happen when I’m at home or in my office. All of a sudden the place feels unreal, and it’s like I’m watching myself from across the room instead of actually being there.
Since the incident with him, have you been having unwanted, vivid memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about what happened?
I’m not really sure what counts as a flashback. I do think about it, but I can’t say I’ve had vivid memories or nightmares exactly.
How long ago did the incident with him occur?
About two weeks ago. It started after that client threatened me in my office.
Since the incident, have you noticed feeling unusually on edge, easily startled, or having trouble sleeping or concentrating?
Yeah. Even at home in Roanoke, I’m tracking every car door, every footstep on the porch, and where the exits are. It feels like I need to be ready in case someone comes at me again.
Since the incident, have you found yourself avoiding certain people, places, or situations that remind you of what happened?
I haven’t really noticed myself avoiding anything in particular.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient developed dissociative symptoms (depersonalization - feeling detached/watching self from outside), a gap in memory for part of the traumatic event, and hyperarousal/hypervigilance beginning immediately after a clearly identifiable traumatic stressor (client threat) approximately two weeks prior. Symptoms do not meet full PTSD criteria as duration is under one month and there is no clear re-experiencing (flashbacks/nightmares) or avoidance behavior. No evidence supporting panic disorder (no autonomic surge, no fear component) or seizure-related mechanism (no motor symptoms, incontinence, or loss of consciousness). The temporal proximity to trauma (<1 month), presence of dissociative symptoms, and hyperarousal support Acute Stress Disorder (F43.0) as the most fitting diagnosis at this stage, pending reassessment if symptoms persist beyond one month (which would suggest PTSD).
